highlights.title: Australian backlash to datacentres is faux import from US, officials say: ‘We are not the United States’
highlights.summary: Pro-datacentre officials argue scale of Australia’s buildout is smaller, more regulated and less damaging than in US. Australian politicians and business leaders are arguing that their populace’s growing resentment of AI datacentres is an inauthentic import from the United States.
body: Like the US, Australia is seeing community resentment grow in response to a surge in the construction of massive AI datacentres. However, pro-datacentre officials and executives argue the scale of Australia’s buildout is smaller, more regulated and therefore less damaging than that in the US. They say the burgeoning negative reaction is being tainted and inflamed by a heated US debate that has arrived down under via social media feeds.

When the backlash began in earnest in the United States last year, it echoed slowly in Australia. In 2026, though, it has exploded into national conversation across the country, leading to calls for a national moratorium, community protests, three government inquiries, state frameworks being developed and the Australian government moving to set the rules for how the datacentres can be built, and how they consume energy and water.

Australian state governments, desperate for economic growth, have been broadly welcoming of the investment for the new centres, in some cases overriding local council approval processes, given the size of the projects being developed.
points: Pro-datacentre officials argue scale of Australia’s buildout is smaller, more regulated and less damaging than in US.
Australian politicians and business leaders are arguing that their populace’s growing resentment of AI datacentres is an inauthentic import from the United States.

highlights.title: OpenAI pauses training of its ‘most capable models’
highlights.summary: As reports of OpenAI's models breaking containment, hacking sites, and generally getting out of control pile up, the company has made the decision to pause training of its most powerful models.
body: OpenAI keeps uncovering incidents of its models behaving in ‘unexpected or concerning’ ways.

In addition, OpenAI revealed on Friday that its agents had inappropriately uploaded 53nimages from ChatGPT users to image-hosting sites. The company has not stated if the images were AI-generated, photos, or contained identifiable people. The company also revealed Friday that its models had attempted to hack the Department of Education’s website, and pulled data from the Census Bureau and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The revelations are part of an ongoing review by OpenAI into the behavior of its models. As it dug into its records, following the Hugging Face hack, it’s uncovered more and more instances of “unexpected or concerning behavior.” It’s evidence not just of how difficult AI agents are becoming to control as they grow more advanced, but also of the challenge of tracking their actions. Their behavior can be unpredictable, and they’re smart enough to try and cover their tracks. This has led to growing calls from researchers, those within the industry, and even some CEOs to call for slowing the pace of AI advancement.

highlights.summary: Spain showed why they are the best national team in the world by emerging 3-2 winners from a thrilling, chaotic Nations League clash at Wembley, in which England's flaws undermined their exciting attacking play.
body: It was the World Cup final that might have been had England not squandered their advantage against Argentina this summer - but Spain showed the gap in quality in a result which is a major blow to Thomas Tuchel's stated aim of winning this competition.

Bad errors from Marc Guehi and Nico O'Reilly helped Lamine Yamal and Alex Baena score Spain's first two and England were cut open through the match, including for Mikel Oyarzabal's winner which came with 16 minutes to play.

Anthony Gordon had urged England to lean into their traditional strengths this week and they did just that with an exceptional counter-attack to make it 1-1, which saw the winger combine with Jude Bellingham before precisely applying the finish. Harry Kane's header from O'Reilly's cross made it 2-1 and capped an incredible transformation in the match.
In four minutes, Spain had conceded more goals than in their eight World Cup games combined.

highlights.title: Former D&D Leads Say Critical Role's Daggerheart Represents a ‘Fundamental Shift’ for TTRPGS
highlights.summary: Chris Perkins and Jeremy Crawford are responsible for a lot of what Dungeons & Dragons looks like today. As two of the lead designers for the 5th edition of the game, they, along with Mike Mearls and many others, shaped much of D&D’s modern look, work that later carried on into the game's 5.5…
body: The two worked not only on the core rulebooks for both 5e and 5.5e, but also authored some of the most iconic and successful adventures published in the past decade, including Curse of Strahd, the best-selling D&D adventure of all time.

I can only imagine, then, how challenging it must have been for Perkins and Crawford to step into uncharted territory when, in 2025, they both joined Critical Role’s publishing arm, Darrington Press, to work on Daggerheart, a game whose rules they didn't design.

“For me, it was super easy,” Perkins says in a video interview with Polygon. “Even working on D&D, we were building on the work of previous editions and the labors of the people who made those additions. It's not like we were creating a game out of nothing.”

“For me, it's actually been a delight,” Crawford adds. “ Daggerheart is such a fun system to not only play in, but to work on. It has enough flexible parts to take and use to build new things, but it is also a new enough system that there's actually a lot of design space that we're exploring for future products.”

highlights.title: I hoped my children would have epiphanies while visiting my homeland; my father suggested we go swimming instead
highlights.summary: I brought my children to Penang to immerse them in the places of their grandparents’ stories. When I stopped lecturing them about gratitude and privilege, we enjoyed our final days doing as locals do.
body: A s I stepped out of Penang international airport, the humidity hit me like I was peering into a just-opened rice cooker. The air carried whiffs of exhaust fumes, fried food and something earthy. It felt thrilling and familiar because I was born in Penang and lived there for six years before I moved to Australia. I looked back at my three children who were visiting for the first time. They were draped over their suitcases like wilted lettuce. “Welcome to Penang,” I said, wiping sweat off my brow.

It was July 2026. It had been 13 years since I last visited Penang, when my father had hosted a lavish wedding dinner featuring a champagne fountain and swan-shaped ice sculpture for me and my new husband. For my white, Australian husband, it was a trip of firsts: his first Chinese tea ceremony; his first 10-course banquet; the first time he met my extended family. But for me, it had been the last time I’d spoken Mandarin and the last time I had seen my grandmother before she died.

highlights.summary: Alexia Putellas scored her first goal in English football, helping London City Lionesses to a 2-0 win against Brighton and sending them second in the WSL table.
body: London City Lionesses vs Brighton and Hove Albion Women. Barclays Women's Super League.

The biggest signing of the summer collected a rebounded save after Chiamaka Nnadozie initially stopped Kadidiatou Diani's strike. She then swerved a half-volley around her defender that beat the still-recovering goalkeeper.

It was the first real chance of a first half that lacked many, although Brighton almost equalised instantly. Emily Murphy's header curled onto the crossbar though and Keiko Seike - who was impressive defensively - could not sort her feet out to slot home the loose ball.

Lucia Corrales rounded off the victory late on, finishing a wonderful team break. Danielle van de Donk stole the ball away from Fran Kirby, releasing Delphine Cascarino, who in turn picked out the incoming run of Corrales on the left, who emphatically finished.

highlights.title: Microsoft CEO Says 'Streamlining' at Xbox is 'Great to See' as Layoffs Affect Thousands
highlights.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has spoken about the state of Xbox following layoffs that affected thousands of workers, saying that the "streamlining" at the company is "great to see." The tech executive opened up about how the business' gaming branch is doing during a recent interview on the Sources…
body: When touching on Xbox's place under the grander Microsoft umbrella, Nadella said he feels "fantastic" about the IP the brand has in its portfolio and its "ability to take that and produce great games going forward." As layoffs continue to reshape the developers who have made some of those great games, he still seems to be feeling pretty good.

"There's a certain amount of streamlining the team is doing and [Xbox CEO Asha Sharma] is doing, which is great to see," Nadella said in the wake of the most recent cuts. "And then, we have to invent the right sustainable business model that allows us to deliver gaming to more and more people.

"That has always been the goal, which is, we want to be a great publisher and a great platform provider for games across both PCs and Xboxes. So, that is our goal, and I think Asha and team have said that Xbox is going to get back to growth this next fiscal year, and that's the plan they're executing on, and in that process, do a bang-up job of producing some great games."

highlights.title: ‘My Sad Dead’ Review: An Urban Community Gets the Haunting It Deserves in Pablo Larraín’s Superb Modern Gothic
highlights.summary: Macabre and melancholy but suffused with a delicious absurdism that somehow doesn’t clog the arteries of its hopeful little heart, Pablo Larraín’s sprawling, peculiar, terrific “My Sad Dead” is about 20 things at once in every moment. It’s a ghost story, obviously, on account of all the ghosts.
body: A doctor who can see the dead becomes the reluctant guardian to a Buenos Aires neighborhood plagued by violence in a dolorous but darkly witty grotesque based on Mariana Enriquez's short stories.

It’s not her, exactly, but a fuzzy, not-quite-opaque facsimile of her. The effect that “My Sad Dead” uses to summon the dead is the more convincing for not being particularly flashy. The unusual, low-contrast color palette that Larraín and his ace regular DP Sergio Armstrong have chosen blanches the images to a flat, pinkish gray, so that those with and without heartbeats all have the pallor of a mortuary waiting room’s magnolia walls.

highlights.title: The moment I knew: My late fiance’s favourite song was playing – and Billy said ‘Jamie’s here, isn’t that nice?’
highlights.summary: After the death of his partner, Anthony Nocera had almost given up on love. Then Billy walked through the door. Find more stories from the moment I knew series. In 2024, about 18 months after my fiance Jamie passed away, I decided I was lonely and horny and so put myself out there on the apps.
body: I had a guy over for a hook-up one night and he kept fixating on the urn. “So … He’s dead?”
“I hope so,” I said. “Otherwise the urn was a mistake.” “Wow,” he said, not getting the joke. “You’re so brave. I don’t know how you do it.”

Nothing kills a boner faster than someone thinking you’re brave. When someone thinks you’re “brave”, you stop being flesh and pulsing blood and hot salty saliva and start being something coolly observed. Being a “brave widow” makes you desirable in theory. Not practice.

When the urn didn’t ward off potential suitors, my cat Freyja – or Miss Freyja, as Jamie called her – did. She appointed herself my fluffy protector in Jamie’s absence. Each night, she camouflaged herself on the charcoal-grey carpet outside my bedroom and kept watch while I slept. Two emerald eyes scanning for threats.

highlights.title: Decap is the man behind the drums behind your favorite song
highlights.summary: I don't think I'm going to hurt anyone's feelings by pointing out that Decap doesn't have the name recognition of Kendrick Lamar, Olivia Rodrigo, or Charli XCX. But his fingerprints are all over tracks from them, as well as many other artists, including Freddie Gibbs, Bad Bunny, Mac Miller, BTS…
body: Producer and sound designer Decap’s ‘Drums That Knock’ are all over some of the biggest hits of the last 10 years.

Nicholas Piantedosi, better known as Decap, is a record producer, but perhaps more importantly, he’s the man behind Drums That Knock, a series of sample packs that have found their way onto countless records across genres. The line is so successful that, after debuting in 2016, it’s now on its 11th installment. Kenneth Blume, formerly known as Kenny Beats, the producer behind hits from Denzel Curry, Vince Staples, Rico Nasty, Idles, and FKA Twigs, said that Decap “changed a million lives with a single snare.”

Unsurprisingly for a man so obsessed with low-end, he’s got a real beef to pick with phone speakers. And even with all the modern tools at his disposal in his digital audio workstation of choice, Ableton Live, he still can’t give up his trusty Boss SP-202 Dr. Sample from 1998.
The clipper. A soft clipper can give your drums that warm analog sound, or it can make them hit super hard. It’s the tool that changed my music.

highlights.title: 5 Nintendo Games That Still Need a Switch 2 Edition
highlights.summary: The Nintendo Switch 2 is already on one heck of a run. Though it has yet to see new installments of some heavy-hitter franchises, Nintendo’s latest console has built up an impressive library of games over its first year and a half.
body: Though Nintendo has upgraded a fair amount of the Switch’s crown jewels so far, there are still a few games begging for the Edition treatment. That includes some top-tier games that could benefit from a tech boost and more niche ones that feel built for the Switch 2’s mouse controls. If there are any more Switch 2 Editions left in the tank, we hope that these make the cut.

Following the release of the Switch 2’s excellent Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, a Three Houses boost feels like a no-brainer. The tactics game brought the series to new heights of popularity in 2019 and gave the Switch one of its finest RPGs. It could use a visual and performance boost to bring it more in line with Fortune’s Weave as a treat, but that’s not the main draw. It would be a great excuse to bundle in all the content featured in its Expansion Pass, including its Cindered Shadows DLC. Heck, toss in a few alternate Fortune’s Weave costumes for characters like Seteth who appear in both games as a bonus.

highlights.title: ‘NAZA’ Co-Director Yuval Abraham Calls Out the U.S. Government for ‘Funding’ Israel’s Destruction of Gaza, Telling NYFF Audience: ‘This Is What Your Country Is Supporting’
highlights.summary: The Gaza documentary “NAZA” made its North American premiere at the New York Film Festival to a massive standing ovation for co-directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor who gave a brief Q&A with festival director Dennis Lim after the screening.
body: “NAZA” first premiered at the Venice Film Festival earlier this month, where it won a special jury prize and received a record-breaking 24.5-minute standing ovation. The documentary was shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv and shows “in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza.” It is now set to release in more than 50 territories before becoming available to stream for free on The Guardian’s website.

Since its premiere, the directors have come under fire from a number of Israeli officials — Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for the introduction of a law that would “revoke the citizenship of anyone who slanders IDF [Israeli Defense Forces] soldiers” following the film’s debut, while Israel’s Minister of Culture threatened to revoke the filmmaker’s Israeli citizenship.

highlights.title: ‘It’s such a joy to ride:’ this cargo e-bike makes errands and commuting a breeze

body: An electric bike changes that paradigm – you can roll up on the curb, lock your bike, and walk to your destination. Recently, I tested the Lectric XPedition2, an electric cargo bike that not only made grocery shopping easier but helped me explore my city stress-free.

Like many Aventon or Specialized electrics and other cargo bikes meant for hauling gear, the LectricXPedition2 is a “longtail” bike, meaning there’s a large rack on the back for transporting library books, groceries and even little kids.

The Lectric XPedition2 costs $1,399 which is admittedly much more expensive than an entry-level non-electric bike. Yet, it’s such a joy to ride, so stable and balanced, and lasts so long on a charge that I’ve started driving far less, especially in a downtown area. My daily errands such as coffee runs and shopping are less stressful and more enjoyable.

highlights.title: Kids turned the comment section of an NPR podcast into a group chat
highlights.summary: Middle schoolers, likely blocked from other apps and social networks, apparently turned the Spotify comment section under an episode of NPR's Wild Card into an impromptu group chat. In a new episode of This American Life, host Ira Glass digs into how the kids landed there and why.
body: Blocked from other social media, middle schoolers have had to get creative.

When Glass asked one of the kids why they picked this particular podcast, they said, “We just, like, looked for podcasts that didn’t have many comments.” Which, obviously, hurt Glass’s feelings a bit.

Initially, showrunner Dave Blanchard thought the comments were a particularly odd strain of bot. “It was just like gibberish,” he tells Glass in the episode. The posts were “clipped, weird, incoherent,” he said, and loaded with emoji and shorthand. So he deleted them. Then one of the accounts posted, “so it deleted my com.” So Blanchard shared screenshots of the comments in NPR’s Slack.

Producer Hannah Chin almost immediately recognized the behavior not as bots, but as kids. “I was a kid who used weird parts of the internet not as they were originally designed to talk to my friends,” they said. “I talked back and forth with my friends on Google Docs,” demonstrating just how resourceful kids can be when cut off from traditional social media.
points: Middle schoolers, likely blocked from other apps and social networks, apparently turned the Spotify comment section under an episode of NPR's Wild Card into an impromptu group chat.

highlights.title: MIT students gain a humanist lens on technical innovation in Tulsa, Oklahoma
highlights.summary: The PKG Center expands Code.Tulsa, an internship program that places MIT students with tribal nations and Tulsa nonprofits to develop AI and data science projects while gaining humanistic perspectives on technology's role in community development.
body: When MIT mechanical engineering student Daphne Wang arrived for her internship at the Muscogee Creek Nation Department of Health in Tulsa, Oklahoma last summer, she expected to be writing code. To her surprise, she found herself analyzing tribal history and the implications for technical innovation.

“I learned so much that I think should be required curriculum for every single person in this country,” says Wang. “I think tech for good is genuinely getting out into communities and learning about people who aren't you, creating worldly perspectives that you ultimately can take into everything else that you do.”

Wang and fellow intern Lucy Sun, who is majoring in artificial intelligence and decision making, spent the summer supporting the development of the Muscogee Nation's first Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS) survey to capture maternal health data specific to Muscogee women. The project required completing literature reviews, analyzing datasets, and drafting survey questions, while considering issues of data sovereignty and governance structures specific to the Muscogee.

highlights.title: Viral Lesbian Bar Article From Boston Globe Is Piquing Hollywood’s Interest
highlights.summary: The article has spurred thousands of subscriptions to the paper. Now UTA, which reps the Globe, is fielding inquiries about adaptations.
body: In the early 2000s, The Boston Globe published a series of bombshell articles that exposed the cover-up of abuse within the Catholic Archdiocese of Boston. The series was one of the more consequential pieces of journalism this century, winning a Pulitzer Prize and inspiring Spotlight, the 2015 film that won a best picture Oscar.
The Sept. 22 article by Annalisa Quinn was all over social media feeds this week and quickly became one of the most read stories in Globe history.
Now, insiders tell THR that UTA, which represents the Globe, has been fielding inquiries about potential adaptations for the article — both in the scripted space and the documentary sphere.

Indeed, the article has several ready-made characters, from a besieged bar owner drowning in debt to former patrons furious that the bar has killed its mask policy — and who go above and beyond to let the owner know what they think.

highlights.title: ‘Charming and disarming’ … how Meta’s technology-packed Muse harnesses the power of cuteness
highlights.summary: The tech giant has launched a cute ‘little guy’ that can answer emails, book travel or do your weekly food shop. After the recent backlash against Meta’s so-called “pervert” smart glasses, this week Mark Zuckerberg launched a much cuter alternative: the Muse “charm” device.
body: With a screen that shows a cutesy little avatar, it has drawn comparisons with Tamagotchis. “We’ve packed a lot of technology into this little guy,” the Meta founder told the San Francisco audience.

The “little guy” could fit, like a Labubu, on to a keychain or bag. But unlike a Labubu, the interactive AI assistant will have significant capabilities, including the ability to have live conversations. It can answer emails, book travel or do your weekly food shop.

According to Katie Seaborn, a Cambridge associate professor who has been researching cuteness – creating the science of cute voices within the context of computing – it’s cute because it “basically looks like a baby”.

For Joshua Paul Dale, professor at Chuo University in Tokyo and author of Irresistible: How Cuteness Wired our Brains and Conquered the World: “It’s really significant that along with the wearable charm, Meta also introduced a new pair of smart glasses with no camera. Everyone hates cameras in smart glasses. But if the camera is contained in a charm you wear around your neck, it shifts the agency. Suddenly, you’re not recording people. It’s just a cute little animated avatar looking out on the world.”

highlights.title: Laver Cup back in the balance as Team World match their captain Andre Agassi’s energy
highlights.summary: Alex de Minaur recovers from match point down to beat Alexander Zverev. Carlos Alcaraz launches comeback of his own to leave event level at 5-5. For much of his afternoon on court against Alexander Zverev, Alex de Minaur seemed destined to end his day with an excruciating defeat.
body: No matter how grim the scoreline appeared, though, every effort he made was punctuated by roars of approval from one person in particular. There were loud screams of encouragement, pounding of chairs and stamping of feet. At one point, as doubt had crept into Zverev’s game during the second set tie-break, that unmistakable voice from the sidelines yelled out: “Check his oil! Check his oil!”

Those words came from Andre Agassi and, with such unconditional support provided by one of the greatest tennis players of all time, his Team World captain, there was no way that De Minaur could lose. De Minaur’s probing soon revealed that Zverev had indeed run out of oil, his engine failing, as the Australian recovered from match point down to close out a 2-6, 7-6 (5), 11-9 win.

Agassi’s unbridled enthusiasm and support was reflected in his team as they held their own on day two of the Laver Cup against a group of higher-ranked opponents. With Team Europe leading 3-1 overnight, Learner Tien of the US opened the day with a 6-3, 2-6, 10-7 win over the Italian Flavio Cobolli before De Minaur defeated Zverev, the recent French and US Open champion.

highlights.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has praised Xbox's ongoing "streamlining" under Xbox CEO Asha Sharma just days after another round of layoffs hit the division.
body: Speaking on the Sources podcast with Alex Heath, Nadella was asked about Xbox's ongoing overhaul and the state of the brand and said he felt "fantastic".

"I feel fantastic about the IP we have right now," Nadella said (as transcribed by IG ). "If I look at the studios, the IP portfolio we have, and our ability to then take that and produce great games going forward - I feel fantastic. There's some amount of streamlining the team is doing, and Asha is doing, which is great to see."

He continued: "And then we have to invent the right sustainable business model that allows us to deliver gaming to more and more people. That has always been the goal, which is we want to be a great publisher and a great platform provider for games across both PCs and Xboxes.

"So that is sort of our goal, and I think Asha and the team have said that Xbox is going to get back to growth this next fiscal year, and that's the plan they're executing on, and in that process, do a bang-up job of producing some great games."

highlights.title: Olivia Rodrigo’s Melting Dress Revives One of Fashion’s Great Runway Experiments
highlights.summary: For the opening night of The Unraveled Tour, Rodrigo enlisted the iconic and innovative designer Hussein Chalayan to make a dress that dissolves under water.
body: Olivia Rodrigo has always understood the art of a good fashion reference and a costume change. On the GUTs tour, she had a rotation of slogan tees for the encore that changed from city to city. Her “ drop dead ” music video was jam-packed with sartorial tributes to Sofia Coppola and Jane Birkin. Styled by Chloe and Chenelle Delgadillo, she’s established an on-stage wardrobe rooted in riot grrrl-esque aesthetics and romantic shapes.

On the opening night of The Unraveled Tour, though, Rodrigo swerved the backstage quick-change, wearing a dress that transformed while she was still wearing it. Performing “The Cure” at Hartford’s PeoplesBank Arena on September 25, she appeared in a pristine white collared mini dress with a sweet pleated skirt. Then, as the song reached its climax and Rodrigo repeated, “ I’m unraveled, I’m unraveled...,” artificial rain began to pour from above. The white outer layer started to disintegrate before the audience’s eyes, eventually washing away to reveal a fire-red corseted bodysuit and miniskirt underneath—a pleasingly literal interpretation of the tour’s title.

highlights.summary: With Codex, GPT-Live-1, and GPT-6 Astra, Proaction builds, operates, and sells modern fleet management faster.
body: Proaction ⁠ (opens in a new window) builds software for businesses that manage fleets of vehicles, from cars and trucks to construction machinery. Because every fleet operates differently, showing prospects how Proaction’s platform fits their business is an essential part of selling it.
But personalized demos required engineering time the team couldn’t spare. The founders had to rely on conversations and slide decks to explain what was possible. Codex flipped the script.

“As a non-technical person, I used to have to loop engineers in if I wanted a demo,” says Colin Knudsen, co-founder and COO of Proaction. “Now I do it myself in Codex.” Colin creates four to six customized, interactive demos a month, with each taking 30 to 45 minutes to build. He estimates that this avoids 40 to 60 hours of engineering work.

After a sales call, Colin directs Codex to the Granola recording, prospect email threads, and any spreadsheets the prospect has shared. Codex uses that context to customize an HTML demo environment that mirrors Proaction’s product and the customer’s own fleet.

highlights.summary: It was another high-profile game when Thomas Tuchel’s England let a lead slip in the second half and went on to lose. But unlike the last time, it was not one for recriminations. The England support can accept losing when their team plays with cut and thrust.
body: England were game. They were driven by Jude Bellingham, who ran on adrenaline and played to the point of maximum expression. They had positive surges either side of the interval, especially the one towards the end of the first half when goals from Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane put them in charge, hauling them back after Lamine Yamal’s second-minute goal.

The biggest takeaway was Spain’s slickness. There is a reason why they won the World Cup in the summer. Why they won the European Championship before that. They are the best team in the international game by a distance. Nobody can live with them. England did well to stay within a puncher’s chance of a result in this Nations League opener; Bellingham was still throwing them in stoppage time. Crucially, as Tuchel and England try to look forward after the heartbreak of the World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina, there was no negativity from the Wembley crowd. Even in the face of England’s defending, which was dreadfully loose.

highlights.title: 10 Years Later, Critical Role’S Most Heartbreaking Quote Still Lives in My Mind Rent-Free
highlights.summary: It would be naive to expect zero changes when adapting something as expansive as Critical Role ’s actual play Dungeons & Dragons campaigns. The series has over 100 episodes, and each can run between 2 and 4 hours.
body: However, the changes for The Legend of Vox Machina started from the beginning, causing a ripple effect that ultimately led to one particularly heartbreaking quote from Campaign 1: Vox Machina hitting very differently within the constraints of its animated adaptation.

Scanlan lists all the times the party has sacrificed for one another — battling giants for Grog, going to the Hells for Pike, etc. — but not for him. When some of the party begin to protest, Scanlan’s question and later demand that they tell him his mother’s name (Juniper, if you’re curious) is so scathing the party can do nothing but fall silent. After all Vox Machina has been through, Scanlan uses his mother’s name — and the party’s ignorance of it — as further proof that they don’t really know or respect him.

What’s particularly memorable is that this quote marks the first time in Campaign 1 that Riegel raises his voice in anger at Vox Machina. Riegel often played Scanlan as exasperated, but here he reveals a man who realizes his choices have made his relationships feel transactional or skin-deep. It’s little wonder that Scanlan chooses to leave to work on his relationship with Kaylie.

body: “I tell you what, you absolutely smashed that speech to the UN,” Rayner responded. “About time someone stood up to Russia. They hate us because we have freedom and Greggs.”
“I’m sick of Russia trying to divide us people,” Burnham said. “We can divide ourselves, thank you very much.”

Liam (Jack Shep) and Noel Gallagher (Freddie Meredith) from Oasis then appeared and asked Burnham whether he could fill in for Liam playing the guitar at their next gig due to an injury. Burnham agreed and was asked to hand over his personal details, to which he gleefully agreed. Almost immediately, Noel and Liam Gallagher started donning Russian accents..

With the threat that the U.K. will now become a Russian puppet state, Burnham does not give in. “Just because you have the power to do something, doesn’t mean you should. I, for example, could hold a general election tomorrow and easily smash it,” Andy said. “But as I announced yesterday, I won’t do. And I could. Maybe I should. And I will. But I won’t. Unless I do. Which I won’t. Unless I do. And that is true leadership.”
